title: Moog sub
notes:
The machine low end. The shelf's four basses are a neutral saw, a fuzz, a Jazz Bass and a double bass — every one of them a *player*, three of them explicitly acoustic. Nothing here can hold the bottom of a house or techno record, where the bass is not played at all: it is a filter, a very low oscillator, and a decay that has to get out of the kick's way and then come back.

Forked from `bass/saw-round` rather than from anything with a body on it, because the point of this voice is the absence of a box. It has **no `body`, no `breath` and no `vibrato`**, and that is a design decision rather than an omission — those three blocks exist to say "a physical object made this", and this object is a voltage. Adding a resonance here would make it a worse synth, not a better instrument.

**A ladder filter, so `mono` and a real filter envelope** — the parent is a bare `synth` with no filter at all, which is why it can only ever be as bright as its oscillator. Base 45 Hz, 3.2 octaves, sustaining at 0.28 with a 180 ms decay: the note opens to about 400 Hz and shuts back down to the fundamental, which is the sound of a sequenced bass line moving. `Q` at 2.4 is the only place on this shelf with real resonance — the ladder's self-oscillation peak is most of what "Moog" means, and every other voice here keeps Q under 1 because a physical body's resonances are supposed to come from `body` instead.

**`fatsquare` at 8 cents, two oscillators.** Square rather than saw: the hollow odd-harmonic spectrum is what sits *under* a four-to-the-floor kick without fighting it, where a saw's even harmonics land exactly where the kick's body is. The 8 cents of detune is the one deliberately un-machine thing about it, and it is there because two perfectly-tuned oscillators sum to one oscillator.

**Attack 4 ms, release 0.18.** Both far shorter than the parent's 20 ms and 0.6. A sub with a slow attack smears the downbeat, and a sub with a long release rings through the next note and turns a bass line into a drone — at 128 BPM the sixteenth is 117 ms, so the release has to be under that or the pattern disappears. This is the one bass on the shelf that is *safe* at fast tempos, which upright-pizz's notes explicitly say it is not.

Sustain 0.55, decay 0.22: enough shape that a held root still has an envelope, low enough that it never pins the mix. Polyphony 2 — a sub line is monophonic in practice, and two voices is the crossfade, not a chord.
summary: Machine sub, resonant ladder filter and no body at all. The house/techno/trap low end, and the only bass safe at fast tempos.
